scaled_manual_segmentation.description: Label-free C. elegans cell-identity annotation from manually segmented nuclei. An identity reference is built from 12 unlabeled pool worms; held-out worms (10 hidden test worms, 4 visible dev worms) are annotated with it, and every nucleus' assigned identity is checked against its biological name (558 nuclei per worm). Scaled from the paper's 100 training / 100 test worms: the paper numbers below are its full-scale results and are not expected at this scale.
scaled_manual_segmentation._scale_note: Paper: 100 training worms (15 for parameter learning, 500 BO trials per stage), 100 test worms. Gym: 12 pool worms (6 for parameter learning, 30/30/10 BO trials), 10 hidden test worms, same 558-nucleus manual segmentations of the Li et al. dataset. Accuracy grows with the number of training worms (paper Fig. 5), so the gym reference sits below 0.961.

atlas_accuracy_mean.description: Mean over held-out worms of the fraction of nuclei assigned their correct biological identity (unassigned nuclei count as wrong).

atlas_accuracy_min.description: Accuracy of the worst held-out worm; rewards methods that annotate every worm well, not only on average.

atlas_accuracy_std.description: Diagnostic: population standard deviation of per-worm accuracy (not ranked).

pre_atlas_accuracy_mean.description: Diagnostic (hidden side only): accuracy of the submitted pool correspondences themselves, i.e. the fraction of pool nuclei whose correspondence group carries their name (not ranked).

gap_to_supervised_oracle.description: Diagnostic: fixed supervised comparator's mean accuracy minus the method's mean accuracy on the same worms (not ranked; the comparator is frozen in eval/, so this is a shifted copy of the primary metric).
